method: Each line of the pasted dump is read as a field name, a colon, a whole number and an optional kB unit; blank lines and # comments are skipped, a field that appears twice is refused, and a value in any other unit is refused. MemTotal and MemFree are required, and MemFree or SwapFree above its total is refused as inconsistent. Total RAM is MemTotal. In use is MemTotal minus MemAvailable, the figure free(1) documents for its used column; a dump without MemAvailable takes available as MemFree plus Buffers and Cached and in use as MemTotal minus that, which is the fallback for kernels before 3.14. Buff/cache is Buffers + Cached + SReclaimable, matching the cache and buff/cache columns of free(1), and shared memory is Shmem. Kernel stacks and page tables add KernelStack, PageTables and SecPageTables when the kernel reports them. Swap in use is SwapTotal minus SwapFree. Every share is that field divided by MemTotal, or by SwapTotal for the swap rows, rounded half up to one decimal; an exact half therefore reads up, not to even. The RAM bar partitions MemTotal into in use and available and the swap bar partitions SwapTotal into in use and free, so each bar adds to exactly its total. Sizes are shown in KiB, MiB or GiB by magnitude, with GiB at two decimals. The page reads only the text pasted into it: it does not query the host, so cgroup limits, watermarks, zswap and reclaim behaviour are not modelled, and a field the dump omits is not invented. Nothing here is a diagnosis of the machine or a recommendation to change it. Everything runs in the browser; nothing is sent, stored or uploaded.
